name: session-receipts
description: pytest-quint-connect checking itself: every real pytest session leaves a results.json status and exit code that describe that session honestly.

actions.init: copy examples/lru_cache into a fresh project directory; no receipt yet
actions.session: run `python -m pytest` in the project with the installed plugin and the options for this kind; read results.json and the exit code
actions.inspect: read results.json and the last exit code without running anything

mutants.name: filtered-counts-as-complete
mutants.description: a -k run that skipped cases is judged as if every case ran

mutants.name: replay-counts-as-complete
mutants.description: replaying one saved trace no longer marks the session incomplete

mutants.name: failed-session-keeps-old-receipt
mutants.description: a failed or still-running session leaves the previous results.json in place

mutants.name: require-complete-ignored
mutants.description: --quint-require-complete is accepted but never changes the exit code

limits: One inner project (the LRU example), five session kinds, both values of --quint-require-complete, at most three sessions per sampled history.
Interrupted sessions (a killed pytest process) are not modeled; only a session that ran to its end.
Mutants patch the installed plugin in each inner pytest process; they are not edits of the source files.
